 Published  November 3, 2026 5:00 PM PST The Brief
 Incumbent Sheriff Robert Luna and former Sheriff Alex Villanueva face off in a high-stakes rematch to lead the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department. 
 Luna bases his platform on constitutional policing, transparency, and violent crime reduction, while Villanueva advocates for aggressive enforcement, rapid deputy hiring, and operational independence. 
 While both candidates emphasize restoring stability, voters must weigh contrasting philosophies on civilian oversight, deputy staffing shortages, and departmental reform. 
 LOS ANGELES - In Los Angeles County's high-profile and fiercely competitive race for Sheriff, incumbent Sheriff Robert Luna and former Sheriff Alex Villanueva are facing off yet again in a showdown for leadership of the nation’s largest sheriff’s department.
 >>Tap or click for live results<< 
 By the numbers:
 Here's a live look as results come in: 
 Candidates at a glance
 Robert Luna 
 Incumbent Sheriff Robert Luna, who was elected in 2022 after serving 36 years with the Long Beach Police Department – including seven years as Chief of Police – is pitching a platform centered on reform, accountability, and stability. 
 Raised in East Los Angeles , Luna's re-election campaign focuses on restoring public trust through constitutional policing, strong civilian oversight, and anti-deputy gang policies. 
 One-on-One with L.A. County Sheriff Robert Luna 
 We talked to Sheriff Luna about everything from the Governor's new law to ban the use of shock gloves to new fire safety equipment for the LASD.
 His core priorities emphasize using data-driven enforcement strategies to reduce violent crime , as well as collaborating directly with county supervisors and local community organizations to address homelessness and public safety.
 Alex Villanueva
 Former Sheriff Alex Villanueva, who served as LA County Sheriff from 2018 to 2022 and spent over three decades rising through the department's ranks as a deputy, sergeant, and lieutenant, is campaigning on a platform of operational strength and aggressive enforcement. 
 Villanueva’s primary goal is to address severe departmental shortages by rapidly hiring 2,000 new deputies to halt forced overtime. 
 Former L.A. County Sheriff Alex Villanueva shares why he wants his job back 
 Former L.A. County Sheriff Alex Villanueva is stepping back into the political arena. 
 Positioning himself as a fiercely independent outsider willing to fight back against county oversight boards and local politicians, his campaign promises to re-establish specialized units to crack down on retail theft, street takeovers, and property crimes across the county.
 A battle over strategy, oversight, and morale
 As the campaign reached its climax, the debate centered on contrasting leadership styles and law enforcement philosophies, with Luna pressing for his record of reform, increased transparency, and a stabilized relationship with oversight bodies.
 Rooted in his upbringing in East LA as the child of a poor Latino immigrant family, Luna’s platform is shaped by experiencing both "good and bad policing" in the very neighborhoods patrolled by the sheriff's department. 
 Grounding his re-election bid on five core pillars—reducing violent crime, increasing public trust, modernizing department infrastructure, addressing homelessness, and improving deputy wellness—he emphasizes steady, relationship-based policing. To advocate for continuing his track record centered on modern leadership and departmental stability, Luna points to sustained year-over-year drops in violent crime across LASD-patrolled communities, alongside his 36-year law enforcement career and seven years as Long Beach Chief of Police.
 LASD Sheriff Luna addresses deputy gangs 
 LASD Sheriff Robert Luna speaks out on deputy gangs and details the actions being taken to eliminate them from the department.
 On the other hand, Villanueva is framing his campaign around the core mantra, " Rescue. Rebuild. Restore, " grounding his platform on his prior accomplishments leading the nation's largest sheriff's department. 
 His campaign underscores his track record of turning a inherited $101 million budget deficit into a $74 million surplus, hiring 1,100 deputies in his first year, and replacing a political patronage system with merit-based promotions. 
 Highlighting his leadership during the 2020 civil unrest, large-scale raids on cartel-tied illegal cannabis grows, and specialized Public Corruption Unit investigations, Villanueva points to his executive and military background—including service in the U.S. Air Force and National Guard—to argue that he possesses the proven crisis management experience required to restore operational strength, financial discipline, and public safety across Los Angeles County.
 LA County Sheriff candidate Alex Villanueva talks top voting issues 
 Eight challengers have entered the sheriff’s race as the filing deadline arrives for the June 2 primary, which includes contests for the Board of Supervisors and Assessor. 
 The Source: This report is based on candidate statements, official campaign positions, and documented career records detailing the platforms of incumbent Sheriff Robert Luna and former Sheriff Alex Villanueva. Information regarding departmental history, public statements, and policy priorities reflects the attributes provided by both campaign teams and departmental records.
